attBesluta.text: Amazing time saver. Wish I had this 10 years ago. Multiple dies can be purchased fairly cheaply. Pays for itself the first job.

Wicked little punch for the price. Doing a commercial construction project that I need to hang various lengths of angle iron. Rather than paying for take off and fab cost decided to buy 20' sticks and fab onsite. Punching 1/4" and 3/8" angle iron. So far ~200 holes flawless. I'm about half done. The ch70 and ‹REDIGERAT› 750w 10k psi Vevor hydraulic pump paired beautifully plug and play and are paid for in the cost of having the iron fab'd by a shop. And I'll have a punch for future. WELL worth the price. Punch a hole in 5-10 seconds vs minutes drilling, I'd probably have spent at least half the cost on drill bits.
will punch a 3/4 hole though 1/4 plate all day long when paired with vevor air hydraulic pump. saves alot of time drilling
Did as advertised outside of the box. Worked first time. Alot of flex when pressing but it's expected.
Haws. After 2 years in my commercial fab shop it still punches with the original dies. Has paid for itself 100 times over literally! Wish I could find replacement dies for it in different sizes.

This thing is stout. No Regerts! Would like to have larger and smaller dies. It will punch more than 3/8 mild steel. It is quite heavy to move but my neighbors love it just as much as I do. Great addition to any home shop.

I bought this roller to roll 2"×1/4" aluminum flat bar the easy way, as it was the most affordable option. With a 3D-printed slip-on roller cover, I was able to match the exact profile I needed to keep the flat bar rolling evenly. It worked flawlessly for my application. Bending this material isn't overly difficult to begin with, but I needed a consistent, clean curve, and after some searching, this proved to be the most economical solution for the job.

pros:is a very solid machine, easy to use if you don't have some industrial repetitive work (hundreds of pieces). spin the handle and the pipe is bending. cons: for long pieces of pipe the machine will bend them slightly out of center, they have to be rectified after.the rollers for flat pieces have two rings with unfortunately one screw each. they will not stand with the setting until you finish the job no matter how hard you squeeze that screw. it can't bend 60/40/2 mm only 50/40/2 max witch is a BIGGG thumb down for it's size. there are smaller home made machine who do that.another conn is that the axel of the wheels use blocking nuts, everytime you change to another position you'll have to use other tools not the bear hand.the axel of the handel is locked with a safety ring and you have to have a special plyers to unlock it. overall is a nice machine to have as a first bender or to use it as a model to build your own to your particular needs.
